summary:
The system starts with a simulated butterfly that provides the input signals. These signals pass through the signal and duty-cycle processing section and are then processed by the AI chip. The processed signals are connected to the TX and RX (Transmitter and Receiver) section, which demonstrates signal transmission and reception. The coil arrangement represents electromagnetic principles, while the battery supplies electrical energy to the motor system. The display and scope blocks are used to monitor output values and analyse signal waveforms.
This project helps us understand how Artificial Intelligence, electronic circuits, communication systems, and motor technology can work together. It also provides practical knowledge of simulation, signal processing, and component integration.
In conclusion, this project provides a basic understanding of AI-based electronic systems and their applications in robotics, automation, wireless communication, and intelligent control systems. It can be further improved by adding advanced AI algorithms, sensors, and automatic control features.
